patchSeries.title: R2 bounded WebSocket worker runspace (accept-loop starvation repair)
patchSeries.thirdFix: run 40084261133 exposed a worker-slot leak: the F99 pump only issued a Read when bytes were already available, so a peer FIN with no pending frame was never observed and the gate slot was held until the idle timeout; added a non-blocking Socket.Poll(0, SelectRead) liveness probe that treats Poll-true + Available==0 as EOF/reset and breaks to the worker finally (release/close/dispose). An 11th static assertion pins Poll+SelectRead.

r2Repair.approach: offload only the long-lived /ws pump to a bounded runspace pool behind a non-blocking SemaphoreSlim; ordinary HTTP stays inline so all script-scope shared state keeps single-threaded semantics
r2Repair.admission: GHRDP_WS_MAX_CLIENTS default 16 clamped 4..64; Wait(0) non-blocking; over-capacity answered 503 and closed
r2Repair.sharedStateSafety: worker receives only the pump dependency surface; no RdpTokens/credential-ledger/cache access; per-connection token validated in the pump; audit serialized on a shared Monitor lock; socket/stream/gate released in finally; reaper + shutdown dispose pool and semaphore
r2Repair.frozenThresholds: scripts/candidate/real-backend.js R2_THRESHOLDS (declared before any run; never adjusted post-failure)

slotReclaimFix.defect: worker-slot leak / zombie workers (run 40084261133): gate drained to count=0/avail=0 while only 3-5 sockets were actually held; 18 audit lines all "ws 503 saturated count=0 avail=0", zero worker EXCEPTION and zero close lines
slotReclaimFix.rootCause: the F99 pump guarded NetworkStream.Read behind ($Client.Client.Available -gt 0 -or $Stream.DataAvailable); on a peer disconnect with no buffered bytes no Read is ever issued, so Read returning 0 (EOF) is unreachable and the worker sleeps until F99WsIdleTimeoutSec instead of releasing its SemaphoreSlim slot promptly
slotReclaimFix.fix: at the top of each pump iteration call $Client.Client.Poll(0, [System.Net.Sockets.SelectMode]::SelectRead); when Poll returns true and Available is 0 (and no buffered stream data) the peer has half-closed/reset, so break with close status 1006 into the existing worker finally, which closes the socket, disposes the stream/runspace handle via the accept-loop reaper and calls SemaphoreSlim.Release()
slotReclaimFix.compatibility: System.Net.Sockets.Socket.Poll exists on .NET Framework (PS 5.1) and .NET (PS 7); Poll(0) is non-blocking; an idle open socket returns false and keeps the original wait behavior; no timeout change, no capacity increase, gate control flow untouched
slotReclaimFix.staticGuard: 11th r2 assertion requires the Poll(0, SelectRead)+Available-eq-0->1006 pattern; passes on LF and CRLF

attempts.newSymptom: every /ws ended in ECONNRESET with an empty body before any 101; held=0, okCycles=0; ordinary HTTP stayed fast (health median 50ms), stall 3818ms->1049ms
attempts.rootCause: Invoke-ClientRequest outer try/finally disposes the stream and closes the client on every return. The async /ws dispatcher returns immediately, so that finally tore the socket down before the worker wrote 101; the inline baseline never hit this because the pump blocked inside the try for the socket lifetime.
attempts.fix: added an r2Dispatched ownership flag set true on the /ws branch and guarded the outer finally with if (-not r2Dispatched); the worker finally remains the single owner that closes/disposes/releases. Worker catch now logs [LAB-R2] worker EXCEPTION instead of swallowing it; a 10th static assertion pins the guard. 0003 is now 509 lines.
